newsitem.title: JAPAN: Toyota targets India market with new car venture.
newsitem.headline: Toyota targets India market with new car venture.

text.p: Japanese auto giant Toyota Motor Corp said on Monday it hopes to grab a slice of the promising Indian auto market through a joint venture to produce and sell multi-purpose vehicles for large Indian families.
"The Indian market has great potential. At this point, we want to create demand for vehicles designed for large families that carry lots of luggage," a Toyota spokesman said.
Earlier on Monday, Toyota announced it had agreed to set up a joint venture with firms in the Kirloskar Group, India's leading engineering group.
The carmaker also said it was awaiting approval for the project from the Indian government.
Total investment in the venture, Toyota Kirloskar Ltd, would be $170 million, and the company is expected to begin production at the end of 1999, Toyota said in a statement.
The venture expects to produce 50,000 vehicles a year, Toyota said.
The spokesman said the names of the companies involved and the breakdown of the stakes held by each party would be released once government approval is granted.
Toyota Kirloskar will be the second joint venture the Japanese carmaker has set up in India, after light commercial vehicle maker DCM Toyota Ltd.
Toyota gave up its stake in DCM Toyota in September 1996, however, when it sold its stake to South Korea's Daewoo Corp .

Analysts in India have said, however, that the Toyota venture's vehicles may be too high priced to compete with local producers. They doubted Toyota would manage to sell more than 20,000 vehicles a year.

An equal-partnership venture between Japan's Suzuki Motor Corp and the Indian government, launched a decade before the start of economic reforms, currently has a share of more than 70 percent in India's passenger car market.

India's passenger car market, opened to foreign participation under a liberalisation programme launched in 1991, has already attracted world majors like Ford Motor Co , General Motors Corp and Daewoo Corp.
